svg.title: Exponential Smoothing vs the Kalman Filter
svg.desc: Smoothing rules let you choose the weights; the Kalman filter lets the model and the noise ratio choose them. At steady state the two coincide.
svg.text: Exponential Smoothing vs the Kalman Filter
A rule where you pick the weights vs an estimator where the model picks them
Rules of thumb or grid search
Trend and seasonality need separate rules
computed from the noise ratio q = Q/H
P and the forecast interval come out together
the steady-state gain is exactly λ
The weight on past observations is fixed
Weights stay fixed until you change λ or the window
The gain moves on its own toward its steady state
It leans on data at first, and widens again after a gap
The value freezes during the gap
No interval, so you cannot tell how much you do not know
It predicts through the gap and the band widens
When data returns, the band narrows again
Smoothing rules let a person choose the weights; the Kalman filter lets the model choose them.
At steady state the two become the same formula — what differs is where λ comes from, uncertainty, and missing data.
The steady-state gain of the local level model
is exactly the λ of exponential smoothing
Next: when the state is a handful of regimes rather than continuous — HMM.
